questions.stem: A kettle operates at 230 V and draws a current of 10 A. What is the power of the kettle?
questions.explanation: Using P = IV = 10 x 230 = 2300 W (or 2.3 kW). This is a typical power rating for a kettle. Option A (23) divides V by I. Option B (240) adds V and I. Option D would come from multiplying incorrectly. A 2.3 kW kettle is realistic for UK mains.

questions.stem: A 60 W filament lamp and a 10 W LED lamp both produce similar amounts of light. Which statement is correct?

options.text: The filament lamp is more efficient because it uses more power
The LED lamp is more efficient because it produces similar light using less electrical power
The filament lamp produces more light because it has higher power

questions.explanation: The LED produces similar light output for only 10 W of input power, compared to 60 W for the filament lamp. The LED is therefore much more efficient — it wastes less energy as heat. The filament lamp wastes most of its 60 W as thermal radiation (heat). Using more power (option A) does not make something more efficient; efficiency is about useful output per unit input.

questions.stem: A current of 3 A flows through a 20 ohm resistor. What power is dissipated in the resistor?
questions.explanation: Using P = I squared x R = 3 squared x 20 = 9 x 20 = 180 W. Option A (60) uses P = IR instead of I squared R. This is a common error — forgetting to square the current. Option B divides R by I squared. Always remember to square the current when using P = I squared R.

questions.stem: An appliance has a power rating of 2000 W and operates on 230 V mains supply. What fuse should be used: 3 A, 5 A, or 13 A?
questions.explanation: First calculate the operating current: I = P/V = 2000/230 = 8.7 A. The fuse must be rated just above the normal operating current. A 3 A or 5 A fuse would blow during normal operation. A 13 A fuse is the correct choice — it allows the normal 8.7 A to flow but will blow if a fault causes excessive current. Always choose the next fuse rating above the operating current.

questions.stem: A 12 V car headlight has a resistance of 2.4 ohms. What is the power of the headlight?
questions.explanation: Using P = V squared / R = 12 squared / 2.4 = 144 / 2.4 = 60 W. Alternatively, find I first: I = V/R = 12/2.4 = 5 A, then P = IV = 5 x 12 = 60 W. Option A (28.8) comes from V x R. Option C (5) is the current, not the power. Option D (14.4) comes from V squared / (R x something). Always choose the most appropriate power formula based on the given quantities.
